currentFormalSemantics.mechanism: scoreCandidate returns immediately at the first failing gate in fixed source order.
notEquivalentTo: marginal causal contribution of that gate
number of stocks uniquely excluded by that gate
counterfactual selected count if that gate were removed

fixedSyntheticWitness.conclusion: Gate-order reversal changes reason prevalence while the accepted set is unchanged. Therefore first-failure counts are order-dependent attribution, not gate importance.

interpretationRules: Reason counts must be labeled firstFailureCount, never gateRejectCount without qualification.
A zero firstFailureCount does not prove a gate never fails; upstream gates may mask it.
A large firstFailureCount does not prove the gate is the dominant source of candidate scarcity; many rows may fail later gates too.
Moving a gate earlier can raise its first-failure count without changing any eventual accepted row.
Outcome studies on one first-failure cohort estimate outcomes of that ordered-funnel subgroup, not the effect of removing the gate.

gateOverlapObserverSpec.purpose: Measure observable PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN overlap without altering Formal order or pretending bypassed rows are Formal candidates.
requirements: Use the same point-in-time feature row consumed by the scan.
Later gate can be evaluated only when all of its own required inputs and prerequisite derived geometry are valid.
Do not call an observed later PASS a counterfactual Formal pass; upstream rejection still stands.

usefulMetrics: uniqueFailOnlyCount among fully evaluable gate subset
conditional next-failure transition after each first failure, descriptive only
selected/zero-pick sensitivity only via preregistered research replay, never by simple count subtraction
falsification: If observableFailCount nearly equals firstFailureCount for a gate across clean dates, upstream masking is small and first-fail prevalence may be a reasonable descriptive proxy.
If multi-fail overlap is high, do not prioritize gate relaxation using first-failure counts.
Any gate-removal replay must preserve all other rules exactly and remain research-only; it is not evidence by itself without outcomes/costs/OOS.
Data-quality gates stay UNKNOWN when inputs are missing and must not be treated as strategy failures.

governance.observerCapture: Potential Class A only if computed from already-loaded scan inputs, isolated research output, bounded cost, no Formal mutation.
